Monza and Aris Thessaloniki locked horns in a pre-season friendly aimed at sharpening tactical discipline and match fitness. Both managers used the opportunity to experiment with their lineups in a fixture that promised plenty of competitive energy. Aris Take Control On July 30, 2026 , the match unfolded with Aris Thessaloniki looking the sharper of the two sides. The Greek visitors established a commanding rhythm early on, utilizing efficient wing play and a solid midfield anchor to dictate the tempo. Monza struggled to find their passing range under pressure, often finding themselves pinned back in their own half as the visitors searched for openings in the defensive line. The visitors' dominance was eventually reflected clearly on the scoreboard as the match entered its final stages. In the 85th minute, Aris Thessaloniki struck again to extend their lead to 0-3 , effectively putting the result beyond doubt. Their clinical execution in front of goal left the home side searching for answers as the clock ticked down toward the final whistle. A Late Consolation for the Hosts Refusing to end the game without a fight, Monza pushed forward in the dying moments of stoppage time. Their persistence paid off in the 93rd minute when Andrea Colpani found space in the box to fire home a well-deserved goal. While the strike made the score 1-3 , it proved to be the final meaningful action of the game. Aris Thessaloniki secured a morale-boosting victory, while Monza left the pitch with valuable lessons ahead of their upcoming campaign.

The summer sun set the stage for an intriguing friendly between FC Rottach-Egern and the powerhouse Bayern München . Fans gathered to see how the tactical preparations of both sides would unfold on the pitch. A Clinical Second-Half Surge On July 30, 2026, Bayern München took to the field looking to refine their finishing and test their squad depth. After an active start to the match, the Bavarian giants refused to let up their intensity as the game progressed. The scoring onslaught in the second half began in earnest in the 50th minute when M. Cardozo found the net to make it 0-7. Just a minute later, the pressure remained relentless as A. Sieb extended the lead to 0-8, signaling that the visitors were far from finished. The fluidity of Bayern's play was evident in every transition. In the 56th minute, J. Palhinha added his name to the scoresheet to bring the tally to 0-9. Shortly after, in the 59th minute, A. Sieb secured his second goal of the day, making it 0-10 and turning the encounter into a masterclass of offensive positioning against a home side that struggled to stem the tide of attacks. Relentless Pressure and Late Goals As substitutions brought fresh energy onto the pitch, Bayern's dominance only grew stronger. B. Ndiaye struck in the 66th minute, followed almost immediately by B. Assomo in the 67th, pushing the scoreline to 0-12. Despite the overwhelming deficit, FC Rottach-Egern continued to fight for every ball, but the sheer technical quality of the Munich side proved too much to handle. In the final stages of the match, the visitors accelerated once more to put a final stamp on the performance. A. Pavlović scored in the 86th minute, and veteran leader J. Kimmich found the target in the 88th minute. The scoring was finally completed in stoppage time when S. Nuraj made it 0-15 in the 93rd minute, capping off a dominant day of football that highlighted the immense firepower available to the German champions.
